ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and beneficial owners against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions, and the NZ Sanctions Act 2019 domestic consolidated list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval. Continuous monitoring and recency checks within the 90-day due diligence window are required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the Latin alphabet (English or Māori characters including macrons). Non-Latin scripts such as Chinese or Japanese must be transliterated into Latin characters for the registered name. A name must be distinguishable, not misleading, not imply Crown/government connection unless approved, and must not contain restricted words without ministerial or regulatory consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a name reservation, the applicant may request reconsideration in writing within 15 working days. If the rejection is upheld, an application for review may be made to the High Court of New Zealand under section 32 of the Companies Act 1993. A fresh reservation application with a revised name may also be filed on the Companies Office portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a hyper-casual mobile game publisher provided that the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in New Zealand and is able to receive legal documents and notices. A post office box alone is prohibited; the registered office must be a physical address capable of receiving service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 2% per year for a low-risk, non-licensed entity. The probability increases to approximately 15% if an AML/CFT risk flag, sanction hit, or material filing irregularity is identified at incorporation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 5–14 (formation and registration), s 15 (company name restrictions), s 16 (registered office), ss 31–39 (constitution), ss 117–122 (share capital and allotment), ss 128–152 (directors, including the requirement under s 152 of a director resident in New Zealand or an approved jurisdiction), ss 189–199 (records and registers), ss 200–202 (registered office and address for service); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2013 (registration fee); New Zealand Business Number Act 2016, ss 27–34 (automatic allocation of the NZBN); Financial Reporting Act 2013 (financial reporting obligations). The internal designation 'International Company' (CK_IC) is a commercial structuring label; the legal vehicle is an ordinary New Zealand limited liability company formed under the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — administered through the online Companies Register at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Registration of a Company (electronic filing via the Companies Register; accompanied by Form 2 Consent to Appointment as Director, the constitution (if adopted), and shareholder/director identification)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A company may allot one or more shares of no par value (Companies Act 1993, s 117); issued share capital may be nominal. There is no capital duty and no escrow account requirement for an ISIC 5820 software-publishing company under New Zealand law. Non-resident ownership is permitted and no bank escrow of capital is mandated before trading commences.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED

PURSUANT to the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), the board of directors of [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (NZBN [number]) adopted the following resolutions at its first meeting, lawfully convened and held on [date] at the registered office of the company:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: RESOLVED that the allotment and issue of [number] ordinary shares of no par value, being all of the issued shares of the company, to the subscribers whose names are entered in the register of members, be and is hereby ratified, approved and confirmed in all respects, such shares having been subscribed for and paid for (in cash or lawful consideration) in accordance with ss 117 and 118 of the Companies Act 1993, and that the register of members be duly updated.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the company be and is hereby fixed, adopted and maintained at [street address, city, New Zealand], and that the directors ensure that notice of the registered office and any subsequent change is lodged with the Registrar of Companies pursuant to s 200 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: RESOLVED that the address for service of the company within New Zealand be the registered office stated above, in accordance with s 202 of the Companies Act 1993.

4. CONSTITUTION: RESOLVED that the constitution of the company, being the document (if any) filed with the application for registration, be and is hereby adopted, ratified and confirmed as the company's constitution; failing any adopted constitution, the default rules set out in the First Schedule to the Companies Act 1993 shall apply.

5. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS: RESOLVED that [Name of Director 1] and [Name of Director 2] (each satisfying the residency requirements of s 152 of the Companies Act 1993) be and are hereby appointed as directors of the company, each to hold office in accordance with the constitution and the Act, and that each director has executed a consent to act as director for filing with the Registrar.

6. APPOINTMENT OF SECRETARY AND REGISTER KEEPER: RESOLVED that [Name of Secretary], if appointed, be and is hereby appointed as company secretary to maintain the company's registers, records and minutes in accordance with ss 189–199 of the Companies Act 1993.

7. BANKING AND SIGNATORIES: RESOLVED that the company open and maintain bank accounts with [banking institution] and that the directors (jointly or severally as resolved) be and are hereby authorised as signatories; further RESOLVED that the directors are authorised to execute contracts with Google LLC (AdMob) and AppLovin Corporation for advertising-based monetization of the company's hyper-casual mobile games, and to open any e-money, payout or merchant accounts incidental thereto.

8. DELEGATION AND OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that the board may delegate day-to-day management powers to any officer, general manager or committee in conformity with ss 130–139 of the Companies Act 1993, and that all such delegations be recorded in the minute book.

CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY. Certified as a true record by the chairperson: [Signature], [Name], [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration name clearance and NZBN eligibility check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Companies Register online portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) — NZBN Name Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name, is not prohibited or restricted, and does not contravene s 20 of the Companies Act 1993 (offensive names or names implying government affiliation are prohibited). Reserve the proposed name if required, and verify that the intended directors meet the residency and age requirements. Ensure the name includes the word 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and one or more alternative names
Director full legal names, dates of birth, and residential addresses
Director identification documents (New Zealand passport or driver licence, or foreign passport certified for AML verification)
Proposed registered office address in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, the applicant may submit a different distinctive name or apply to the Registrar for a determination. The Registrar will provide written reasons, and the applicant may contest the refusal by writing to the Companies Office or, where applicable, by seeking judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting the constitution and internal governance instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators/shareholders and their New Zealand legal counsel (no registry filing required at this stage; the constitution is filed with the Form 1 application if adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the constitution of the company in accordance with s 33 of the Companies Act 1993, addressing share classes, director powers, indemnity, and shareholder rights. Alternatively, elect to rely on the default rules in the First Schedule of the Act by stating 'No constitution' in the application. Prepare a shareholders' agreement for multi-party ownership, including game intellectual-property ownership, revenue-sharing for ad monetization, and governance provisions.
required_dossiers: Draft constitution (if adopted)
Shareholders' agreement (optional but recommended)
Form 2 — Consent to Appointment as Director (signed by each director)
Memorandum of election regarding constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar finds the constitution non-compliant (e.g., inconsistent name or unlawful provisions), the applicant or company may file an amended constitution by special resolution under s 33(1) of the Companies Act 1993 and re-submit the application; any unlawful provision is severable and may be corrected before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic lodgement of Form 1 — Application for Registration of a Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register (online electronic filing system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 electronically through the Companies Register portal. Enter the company name, names of shareholders and directors, registered office address, address for service, constitution election, and principal business activity (software publishing — ISIC 5820). Attach the signed consents of each director and pay the prescribed registration fee of NZD 92.40 (approximately USD 57). Certify that the information is true and correct, and confirm that at least one director satisfies the residency requirement of s 152 of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Application for Registration of a Company
Form 2 — Consent to Appointment as Director (signed by each director)
Constitution (if elected) as a PDF attachment
Director identification and verification documents
Registered office consent (landlord or principal's consent to use the address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the Companies Office issues a defect notification; the applicant must respond within the stated period (usually 10 working days) by correcting the electronic form and uploading cure documents. If registration is refused, request a written statement of reasons and lodge a fresh application; late filing fees apply only where re-submission is delayed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and automatic allocation of NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the Registrar of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful processing, the Companies Office issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number, and the NZBN Registrar automatically allocates a New Zealand Business Number under the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016. Verify the registration details, download and print the certificate, and retain it for bank account opening, tax registration, and contractual due diligence.
required_dossiers: None to be submitted by the applicant — the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN are generated electronically by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or NZBN is not generated within the service standard, contact the Companies Office helpdesk with the application reference and request re-issuance of the electronic certificate. Any error in company details (e.g., name or address) may be corrected by filing a notice of change under s 24 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation organisational meeting and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (with filing obligations to the Companies Register for any officer changes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first meeting of the board and adopt the First Board Resolution covering share allotment, registered office adoption, officer appointments, banking arrangements, and execution of commercial agreements. Issue share certificates, open the register of members, and record minutes. If the director details were not included in the original registration, or if officers change, file the relevant notices with the Companies Register within 15 working days.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes
Share certificates and register of members
Consent of additional directors/officers (if any)
Resolution of bank signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Register issues a compliance notice for late officer filing, promptly submit the required form and pay any late filing fee; where inadvertence caused the delay, provide a written explanation or statutory declaration to seek remission of the penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with Inland Revenue (IRD number, GST, and employer obligations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (IRD) — electronic services at https://www.ird.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the company's NZBN and incorporation details, register the company for an IRD number for the primary activity of software publishing and digital advertising monetization. Apply for Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration if taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 per annum, or voluntarily to recover input credits, noting that overseas ad-network revenue is subject to New Zealand GST rules regarding remote services. If any employees are engaged, register for PAYE and KiwiSaver obligations and record a workplace accidents-compensation (ACC) cover number in the ACC Business Gateway.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Directors' IRD numbers and identification
Business activity description (ISIC 5820)
Estimated annual turnover declaration for GST register
Bank account details for refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD identifies a mismatch or holds the registration, verify all identifiers against the Companies Register and resubmit; if registration is delayed beyond the service standard, contact the IRD Business Customer Support line and request escalation. Penalties for late GST registration may be remitted on the grounds of reasonable care under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical premises, fire safety, and workplace health-and-safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Authority (local city or district council), Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), and WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure commercial office premises and verify that the building has an up-to-date Building Warrant of Fitness (including the fire safety schedule, means of escape, and emergency lighting). Ensure compliance with the Building Act 2004 and the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Register as a Person Conducting a Business or Undertaking (PCBU) under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015: prepare the workplace safety statement, appoint a health-and-safety officer, and implement first-aid, evacuation, and electrical-safety arrangements. For a pure software-publishing operation, no industrial or manufacturing consent is required.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease agreement
Building Warrant of Fitness and fire evacuation plan
Occupancy approval or Code Compliance Certificate (if new fit-out is undertaken)
Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 compliance statement and risk register
FENZ fire safety record (if the building triggers a fire safety schedule)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Territorial Authority issues a non-compliance notice or infringement notice for building or fire deficiencies, engage a licensed building surveyor to remediate and request a fresh inspection; appeal any notice to the Territorial Authority under the Building Act 2004 or to the District Court. WorkSafe improvement and prohibition notices may be appealed to the District Court within 14 days of issue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board has statutory jurisdiction over ISIC 5820 (software publishing of hyper-casual mobile games) in New Zealand. General regulatory oversight is exercised by WorkSafe New Zealand (workplace health and safety) and the relevant Territorial Authority (building and premises compliance).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence or manufacturing permit is required for the commercial activity of publishing lightweight, ad-monetized mobile games. The company may commence operations upon registration of the company, allocation of the NZBN, and issue of the IRD number; no fit-and-proper licensing gate applies to hyper-casual game publishing in New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is purely digital and office-based with zero physical discharge; therefore, no environmental impact assessment, resource consent, or EPA approval is required under the Resource Management Act 1991. Any premises-related effects are confined to standard commercial-office operations under local territorial authority bylaws.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for production activity: no wastewater, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), industrial effluent, or hazardous waste streams are generated. Office compliance requires adherence to applicable local-authority trade-waste discharge bylaws (if food or beverage preparation areas exist), maintenance of indoor air quality and HVAC systems, compliance with any national environmental standards for heating plant if installed, and environmentally sound e-waste disposal of IT hardware under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and local council e-waste service requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: the subject premises must maintain a Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004, including the building's fire safety schedule and compliance inspection by an Independent Qualified Person (IQP), together with means-of-escape compliance under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Structural load clearance: the existing building must hold an up-to-date Code Compliance Certificate or Building Warrant of Fitness confirming structural adequacy and life-safety design; for leased offices, reliance on the landlord's current warrant of fitness is acceptable. Occupational clearance: under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, the company as a PCBU must provide a safe office workplace, an emergency plan, first-aid provisions, ergonomic workstations, and electrical-safety checks; no special occupational licence is required for game development and publishing staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; secure online portal 'myIR' at myir.ird.govt.nz, with official guidance at ird.govt.nz.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company (CK_IC) that derives New Zealand-sourced income, carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, or becomes liable to register for New Zealand GST (including under the remote-services and imported-low-value-goods rules) must obtain a New Zealand IRD number before or at the time of GST registration. The foreign entity applies using Inland Revenue form IR742 (Registration for Non-Resident Companies) or the myIR online non-resident registration channel, submitting certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, the constitution, the register of directors and shareholders, the registered office and agent details, and a statement confirming the absence of any New Zealand fixed establishment. No minimum capital contribution is required, and no New Zealand-resident director or shareholder is required for a tax-exempt offshore International Company. Upon issuance of the IRD number, the entity registers for GST through myIR using the non-resident supplier (remote services) track if its taxable supplies to New Zealand-resident consumers exceed the NZD 60,000 threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the CK_IC is classified as a tax-exempt offshore International Company: it is not a New Zealand tax resident, maintains no New Zealand fixed establishment or permanent establishment, and its non-New-Zealand-sourced revenue (AdMob and AppLovin advertising payouts) is outside the New Zealand income tax net. The entity nevertheless falls within the New Zealand indirect tax (GST) net to the extent it makes taxable supplies of remote services or imported goods to New Zealand-resident consumers and meets the registration threshold. New Zealand-sourced income, if any, would be subject to New Zealand income tax or non-resident withholding tax under ordinary principles.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a United States-style check-the-box entity election. The available statutory elections and designations include: (i) voluntary GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 before the NZD 60,000 threshold is met; (ii) election to account for GST on the payments basis instead of the invoice basis where the prescribed conditions for non-resident suppliers are satisfied; (iii) the application of the s 11A(1)(k) cross-border B2B zero-rating provision for services supplied to a non-resident GST-registered recipient, supported by the required documentary evidence; (iv) elections and notifications required to neutralise hybrid and branch mismatches under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 (including non-application or consistency elections for a New Zealand branch, offshore controlled entity, or hybrid payer); and (v) for any New Zealand-resident group members, the wholly-owned group election to treat members as a single GST person — generally unavailable to a tax-exempt non-resident IC standing alone.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value-added consumption tax administered by the Inland Revenue Department
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; for non-resident suppliers of remote services and imported low-value goods to New Zealand-resident consumers, the same NZD 60,000 threshold (measured over 12 months) applies to digital supplies such as mobile game ad monetization and in-app content.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory digital stamping, and no API-based prior tax-authority approval for individual invoices. Peppol-based e-invoicing is voluntary. GST-registered persons, including non-resident remote-service suppliers, must file GST returns electronically (normally quarterly) through myIR with any net GST remittance due by the 28th day after the end of the taxable period, and must retain electronic records sufficient to establish the residence of New Zealand consumers and the geo-attribute of each digital transaction; no per-invoice pre-clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a GST-registered CK_IC may zero-rate: (a) exported goods where the goods are exported within 28 days of supply (s 11(1)(a)); (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply (s 11A(1)(a)-(j)), provided the services are not performed directly in connection with New Zealand land or moveable property; and (c) cross-border B2B services supplied to a non-resident GST-registered business under s 11A(1)(k). For hyper-casual mobile games, programmatic advertising inventory sold to AdMob/AppLovin and digital content supplied to overseas users qualify for zero-rating as services rendered to non-residents outside New Zealand, subject to documentary substantiation. Revenue sourced from New Zealand-resident users is standard-rated at 15% once the entity is GST-registered.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window) — required only where physical goods are exported; not applicable to intangible game downloads or pure digital ad monetization
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill — required for physical export shipments; not applicable to digital-only supplies
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statements evidencing receipt of AdMob and AppLovin foreign-currency payouts
Platform payout reconciliation reports (AdMob and AppLovin dashboards) showing the geographic breakdown of users, transaction timestamps, and settlement amounts
Signed ad-network and app-store agreements demonstrating the non-resident status of the counterparties and the offshore location of the service recipients
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess GST within four years from the end of the taxable period (extended to seven years where income was omitted or in cases of gross carelessness, and without time limit for fraud, evasion, or wilful misstatement). Incorrectly claimed zero-rating and undocumented export supplies are clawed back at the 15% GST rate plus use-of-money interest at the statutory underpayment rate. Shortfall penalties under ss 141-141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994 escalate from 20% (lack of reasonable care), 40% (unacceptable tax position), 50% (gross carelessness), and 100% (abusive tax position) to 150% (evasion). Criminal liability may arise under ss 143A and 144A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, with fines up to NZD 50,000 per offence and imprisonment of up to five years for tax evasion; directors, officers, and tax advisors who facilitate fraudulent export zero-rating may be exposed to the promoter penalty and personal liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand - Te Pūtea Matua (monetary authority and prudential regulator); the Financial Markets Authority (AML/CFT conduct supervision and market discipline); the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) for any residual foreign-investment consent thresholds involving sensitive land, rural land, or fishing quota.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates an open capital account with no standalone exchange-control legislation. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. Profit and capital repatriation by a non-resident-owned International Company is unrestricted at the currency-conversion level. The only practical hurdles are ordinary tax withholding (non-resident withholding tax or any applicable double-tax-agreement relief), bank-level AML/CFT source-of-funds verification, and bank-mandated balance-of-payments or statistical reporting requirements for large cross-border transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation exists in New Zealand. There is no mandated timeline for conversion, no minimum conversion ratio, and no requirement to deposit export receipts with a designated domestic bank. A New Zealand exporter may retain receivables in foreign currency and convert at its own commercial discretion. Banks may, however, scrutinise unusual conversion patterns or high-risk transaction flows under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and may report suspicious activity to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a complementary treasury rail, Low as the sole or primary banking relationship. Offshore digital electronic-money institutions (EMIs) are not licensed as New Zealand registered banks and cannot directly access the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) or provide native New Zealand domestic bank account numbers. They may offer multicurrency accounts, card infrastructure, and faster wire routing through a local partner bank or payment aggregator, but New Zealand AML/CFT obligations still require underlying KYC at the participating New Zealand financial institution. A trusted tier-1 New Zealand banking relationship remains necessary for regulated escrow, capital contributions, liquidity management, and final foreign-exchange settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no New Zealand statutory mandate requiring directors of a non-resident-owned International Company to appear physically before bank staff for account opening. Most tier-1 banks permit remote opening through video-enabled KYC and digital signature platforms, subject to enhanced due diligence when the beneficial-ownership chain includes trusts, tax-exempt vehicles, or offshore structures. A face-to-face or additional video interview may be required by bank risk committees if the trust/founding shareholder is complex or if the source of gaming-related digital revenue cannot be fully demonstrated through documentary evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trust-owned International Company with tax-exempt classification and no immediately identifiable physical operating substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing; current trust deed and board resolution appointing the company; an organisation chart tracing all beneficial owners through to natural persons; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; the group's audited or management financial statements; service agreements demonstrating substantive treasury and commercial functions; and a copy of the tax-exempt ruling or statutory reliance document.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume and high-frequency cross-border digital advertising revenue from AdMob, AppLovin, and similar ad-technology platforms tied to a hyper-casual gaming publisher
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed live contracts or developer terms with each ad network; monthly payout certificates and payment history from the ad networks; SDK integration reports or dashboard throughput schedules for the mobile game titles; user-consent and privacy compliance evidence (GDPR, CCPA, and NZ Privacy Act 2020); and expected transaction-profile projections for account monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursements to manufacturers, marketing agencies, or affiliate partners in a wide range of foreign jurisdictions, including third-party payment aggregators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full invoice and purchase-order trail for trade services; supplier onboarding KYC pack containing verified identity, proof of business, and payment instructions; treasury management policy setting expected counterparties, normal payment frequency, and maximum amounts; and a list of the company's high-risk or embargoed-jurisdiction blacklist with transactional rationale for any exception.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Injection of initial capital from an offshore trust jurisdiction using US dollars or other non-NZD currency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital injection; executed subscription or loan agreement specifying amount, currency, repayment terms, and purpose; corporate bank statement from the transferring institution evidencing source account; and a tax clearance, tax indemnity, or DTA residence certificate where bank policy requires.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections should be wired to the beneficiary's New Zealand bank account using SWIFT MT103, or SWIFT MT202 COV for bank-to-bank cover when instructed. Field guidance: Field 50K or 50F contains the remitting account of the corporate parent or trust; Field 56A or 57A identifies the intermediary or beneficiary bank in New Zealand; Field 59 identifies the International Company's account with its New Zealand tier-1 bank; Field 70 should include 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION NZ IC' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN NZ IC' as a clear payment reference. New Zealand does not require a central-bank payment purpose code and does not pre-approve inward remittances. For NZD settlement, cleared funds are credited through the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). For verification, the receiving bank may require an inward remittance certificate, a completed corporate authorisation form, and, for loans, an executed loan agreement. For any transaction involving sensitive land or a material farming asset, confirmation that OIO consent has been obtained or that the OIO exemption applies is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for standard operating payments to suppliers, agencies, and developers. For international goods with documentary assurance, a commercial letter of credit can be issued with SWIFT MT700, amended by MT707, and claimed or settled through MT740 or MT202 under UCP600. For cross-border fund settlement through the New Zealand correspondent network, banks will use MT202 COV. Domestic NZD payments to local service providers can be settled using the high-value ESAS or standard domestic electronic clearing. For ad-network payouts already collected in US dollars, funds can be retained in a USD working account and converted by means of a New Zealand bank FX transaction. All outgoing payments are subject to bank screening, sanctions checks, and the entity's own treasury counterparty whitelist.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot NZD/USD or NZD/foreign-currency transactions for immediate liquidity conversion
Deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts in any fully convertible currency
Rolling or flexible dated FX forwards for matching ad-network payout cycles
Vanilla FX options for premium-based protection without a mandatory future obligation
Cross-currency swaps for converting USD-denominated treasury assets into NZD or other target currency exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the counterparty jurisdiction or underlying commercial exposure cannot support a deliverable forward settlement, subject to documented commercial exposure, ISDA definitions, and bank credit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Compliance Declaration (Form AR-IC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based filing: due on each anniversary of incorporation, with an FSC-prescribed grace period not exceeding six (6) months after the incorporation anniversary; no fixed calendar-year due date applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of approximately 10% of the annual permit fee (approx. US$120) per month or partial month of default; failure to file within 30 days of the anniversary triggers a Registrar's Notice of Default; unrectified default within 60-90 days exposes the company to administrative strike-off and dissolution without court order; directors and the licensed resident agent face individual fines up to NZ$10,000 (approx. US$6,000) for knowingly permitting continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Permit Fee / Corporate Renewal Fee to maintain active registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), collected through the licensed International Company Service Provider
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based payment: annual permit fee payable on or before the incorporation anniversary of each year, concurrent with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment within 30 days of the anniversary triggers an automatic surcharge and accrual of interest; arrears beyond 90 days may result in suspension of corporate privileges and cancellation of the registered office arrangement; arrears beyond six (6) months allow the FSC Registrar to initiate administrative strike-off and dissolution, with publication of the company's defunct status and freezing of any Cook Islands-held assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification and Annual Substance Return (IP-holding and digital publishing activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Economic Substance Division, coordinated with the Cook Islands Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual substance return due within twelve (12) months after fiscal year-end; for a company adopting a 31 March fiscal year-end, the return is due by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed administrative penalty of US$1,000 for failure to file the substance return; sustained default results in the company being listed as non-compliant by the FSC and reported to Cook Islands Inland Revenue, which may withdraw the International Company's tax-exempt status and recapture tax on previously exempt accumulated income

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance Attestation and Beneficial Ownership Register Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), AML/CFT Supervision Unit, and the company's designated Compliance Reporting Officer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, concurrent with the Annual Return filing, within the same six-month incorporation-anniversary grace period; if the company elects a separate compliance reporting period, annually by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual attestation or maintain the Beneficial Ownership Register constitutes an offence under the Cook Islands AML/CFT rules; the company is subject to a fine of up to NZ$10,000 (approx. US$6,000) and each director to a fine of up to NZ$5,000 (approx. US$3,000); repeated non-compliance may result in suspension of the resident agent's authority to act and regulatory strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a standard non-licensed International Company under the International Companies Act 1981-82, as amended. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only if: (i) the company holds a Cook Islands financial services license (banking, captive insurance, or trustee license); (ii) shareholders holding at least 10% of issued voting shares deliver a written demand for an audit; (iii) the FSC directs a financial verification as part of an economic substance review; or (iv) the company's annual gross revenue exceeds US$5,000,000, a threshold used by FSC-regulated agents as an industry benchmark for prudent assurance
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; alternatively, US GAAP may be adopted with the approval of the licensed resident agent where the company's constitutive documents permit. Accounts may be prepared in New Zealand dollars or US dollars and are not subject to public filing unless the company is licensed or the FSC requests a copy

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On an annual basis, and concurrently with the Annual Return, the International Company must file with the FSC a Beneficial Ownership Confirmation identifying every individual who directly or indirectly holds 10% or more of issued shares or voting rights, together with the nature and extent of control. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register within 14 days of the change, and an updated ownership schedule must be transmitted to the FSC through the licensed resident agent. The resident agent must verify and attest the completeness of the filing. Register information is not open to public inspection but is accessible to the FSC, the Cook Islands Financial Intelligence Unit, and, upon lawful request, New Zealand law enforcement under the Realm of New Zealand mutual assistance arrangements
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Directors' Residential Address Register
Register of Charges (mortgages and security interests)
Minute Book (minutes of shareholder and board meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,800 – US$3,500 per annum, depending on the licensed Cook Islands international company service provider and the scope of corporate secretarial, registered office, and AML compliance support engaged
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 in a standard year when no audit is triggered; US$6,000 – US$18,000 for a certified audit or independent financial review if demanded by shareholders, required by a financial services license, or ordered by the FSC

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday; eligible digital-game R&D expenditure may qualify for a 15% refundable R&D tax credit; software development costs and intellectual property amortisation are deductible in accordance with the Income Tax Act 2007; the New Zealand imputation system gives credits for corporate tax already paid so that distributed profits are not doubly taxed at the shareholder level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRD Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via Inland Revenue myIR portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July following balance date; a tax agent extension may defer filing to 31 March of the following year. Provisional tax instalments are due 7 July, 7 October and 7 March of the income year; terminal tax is due 7 April following balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross income from all sources, including AdMob and AppLovin advertising revenue, in-app purchase proceeds, royalties, interest, and other assessable receipts, before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident International Company includes only New Zealand-source income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment or New Zealand business activity; non-resident foreign-source gaming revenue is excluded unless the entity is a New Zealand tax resident under the Constitution Act and case law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses directly incurred in deriving taxable income, including game development labour, cloud server costs, app store commissions, advertising spend, royalties, professional fees, and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may deduct only expenses that are allocated to New Zealand-source taxable income under the source, apportionment, and permanent establishment attribution rules; amounts disbursed to related parties must satisfy arm's-length and economic substance thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Net Taxable Income or Tax Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after allowable deductions and prior-year loss offsets; a loss position is recorded here for carry-forward or possible carry-back application.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter taxable profit or loss after applying continuity and source-matching tests; a non-resident IC with no New Zealand permanent establishment will normally show nil unless it has elected or is deemed to have New Zealand-resident status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 28% applied to Box 3 net taxable income, before application of imputation credits, R&D tax credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same 28% rate to the New Zealand-source taxable income of a non-resident IC; if the IC has no New Zealand filing obligation, enter nil and prepare an NRWT reconciliation where outbound distributions are made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Imputation Credits and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits attached to dividends received, resident withholding tax credits, and any creditable foreign tax paid on thank-you-source or foreign income included in the assessable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC is generally not entitled to New Zealand imputation credits on outbound dividends; however, it may claim foreign tax credits or treaty-based reliefs for income taxed offshore if those income streams are within the New Zealand return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Residual Income Tax and NRWT Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of income tax after credits, or terminal tax payable/receivable; also reconciles dividends paid so that non-resident withholding tax obligations are identified.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must confirm whether NRWT on dividends, royalties, and interest paid to its foreign shareholders or related parties has been deducted and remitted; attach or reference the applicable certificate of residence and treaty relief forms to support reduced rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties of NZ$50 for the first month and NZ$10 per month thereafter, subject to a maximum of NZ$500; late payment penalties of 1% on the first day, 4% on the seventh day, and 1% per month thereafter; use-of-money interest is imposed on all unpaid and underpaid tax at prescribed IRD rates. Deliberate concealment or false statements attract shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax avoided, criminal fines up to NZ$50,000 per offence, and imprisonment for willful evasion.
